subject: Robust SEs with missing = 'listwise' and missing = 'fiml' in general

messages.author: b430763ad49e6cd0
messages.subject: Robust SEs with missing = 'listwise' and missing = 'fiml' in general
parts:
Hi,

I have data on about 120 respondents who filled out a questionnaire (5-point likert-type scale) on 4 seperate time points (t = 0, t = 1, t = 3 and t = 4, in years). 
In my single-factor CFA analysis on one time point, I did the analysis with both estimator = 'ML' and estimator = 'MLM' to observe the difference and whether similar conclusions hold. In 3 out of 4 time points the MLM estimator (and accompanied scaled tests) would give more evidence for a good model (i.e. the scaling parameter > 1). Here everything seemed fine, as ML and MLM didn't seem to differ much. 

If data is missing, it means the respondent didn't answer any of 9 the questions at that time point. If data is not missing, he filled out all questions. The reason why my data are missing is unclear.

Now that I continued to Longitudinal CFA, i.e. using all 4 time points simultaneously, missing = 'fiml' is an option because a respondent may not have answered at t = 1, but he may have done so at t = 3. For example, it could be that the respondent answered at t0, t3, t4 but 'failed' to answer at t1. Hence I want to compare the two options: using missing = 'listwise' (i.e. complete case analysis) and using missing = 'fiml'. I however wonder three things:

1) Using missing = 'listwise' in combination with estimator = 'MLM' or se = 'robust': does this actually work in the sense that you get useful results?
2) When using missing = 'fiml' all my fit indices become terrible. In complete case analysis I get: cfi > 0.99, rmsea <0.04, srmr < 0.04, tl > 0.99, Chisq/ df = 32.886/32, p = 0.327. With missing = 'fiml' this becomes about half that, e.g. cfi about 0.45, chisquare/df = 579.8 / 42, p = 0.000, rmsea > 0.32, ... This is obviously a terrible fit. I wonder why this might happen, why the difference is so huge? 

3) Using robust SEs and / or missing = 'fiml' all my standardized factor loadings become close to 1 (0.98 - 0.99). The correlation between my 4 factors are also almost (but not exactly) 1. So the model converged, but I get really bad results.

Any suggestions why this happens?

Kind regards, 
Amonet

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Robust SEs with missing = 'listwise' and missing = 'fiml' in general
parts: 1) Using missing = 'listwise' in combination with estimator = 'MLM' or se = 'robust': does this actually work in the sense that you get useful results?

Listwise deletion assumes data are missing completely at random (MCAR), which is only realistic if your data are missing by design (e.g., you randomly assigned each person to respond on only 3 of the 4 occasions).

Even if the assumption holds, listwise deletion shrinks your sample, throws useful data away, and lowers your power and precision.  Probably better to use FIML, especially if you can incorporate covariates that explain attrition.

https://academic.oup.com/jpepsy/article/39/2/151/883719

2) When using missing = 'fiml' all my fit indices become terrible. In complete case analysis I get: cfi > 0.99, rmsea <0.04, srmr < 0.04, tl > 0.99, Chisq/ df = 32.886/32, p = 0.327. With missing = 'fiml' this becomes about half that, e.g. cfi about 0.45, chisquare/df = 579.8 / 42, p = 0.000, rmsea > 0.32, ... This is obviously a terrible fit. I wonder why this might happen, why the difference is so huge?

This is evidence against the MCAR assumption.  You are analyzing different data, so the result will differ (1) to the degree that the complete-data sample is not a random sample of the total sample, and (2) with the proportion of missing data and how much missing information they carry (see the article I linked to above about auxiliary variables).

3) Using robust SEs and / or missing = 'fiml' all my standardized factor loadings become close to 1 (0.98 - 0.99). The correlation between my 4 factors are also almost (but not exactly) 1. So the model converged, but I get really bad results. Any suggestions why this happens?

Not sure, but sounds like you need to do some deep digging to find out why the subsample with incomplete data are so different.  Pattern mixture modeling might be necessary to account for non-random missingness.

https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/870b/63b4b3e14ddbf9e9517de0383f19168e69e5.pdf

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Robust SEs with missing = 'listwise' and missing = 'fiml' in general
parts: if you were to run an analysis specifying the estimator as "MLR" and missing as "fiml", would that be the appropriate way to employ the robust fiml approach to handling missing data?

Yes, assuming your data are continuous.  MLM only works for complete data (so listwise deletion), but MLR is an asymptotically equivalent correction that allows incomplete data.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
